title: Ordinal Numbers (1st, 2nd, 3rd) & Birthdays
description: Form and use ordinal numbers for sequence, dates, and answering 'When is your birthday?'.
objectives: Distinguish between cardinal numbers (one, two, three) and ordinal numbers (first, second, third)
Form ordinal numbers up to 31st using suffixes (-st, -nd, -rd, -th)
State dates and birthdays accurately in spoken and written English

sections.title: Ordinal Numbers & Saying Dates
sections.content:
While **cardinal numbers** tell *how many* (one, two, three), **ordinal numbers** tell *position or order* in a sequence (first, second, third).

### Suffix Rules for Ordinals
- Ends in 1 -> **-st** (1st = first, 21st = twenty-first, 31st = thirty-first)
- Ends in 2 -> **-nd** (2nd = second, 22nd = twenty-second)
- Ends in 3 -> **-rd** (3rd = third, 23rd = twenty-third)
- All other numbers (4-20, 24-30) -> **-th** (4th = fourth, 10th = tenth, 11th = eleventh, 12th = twelfth)

### Important Spelling Shifts
- 5: five -> **fifth** (not fiveth!)
- 8: eight -> **eighth** (only one 't')
- 9: nine -> **ninth** (drops the 'e'!)
- 12: twelve -> **twelfth** ('ve' becomes 'f')
- 20: twenty -> **twentieth** ('y' becomes 'ie')

tables.title: How to Say and Write Dates

callouts.title: Saying 'The' and 'Of' in Spoken Dates
callouts.text: Even if written simply as *14 August*, native British English speakers say aloud: **'the fourteenth of August'**.

callouts.title: Preposition for Dates
callouts.text: A specific date ALWAYS takes **ON**: *He was born **on** the 5th of May* (never 'in the 5th of May').

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Cardinals tell how many (1, 2, 3); Ordinals tell order (1st, 2nd, 3rd).
Suffix rules: 1st, 2nd, 3rd; all others up to 20th take -th.
Spelling shifts to memorize: fifth (5th), eighth (8th), ninth (9th), twelfth (12th), twentieth (20th).
Speak dates as 'the [ordinal] of [month]' (the fourteenth of August).
Calendar dates take preposition ON (on the 5th of May).
